title: Euler's identity for a locally finite measure implies the dilation law ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ = sⁿ ∫ g dμ for C¹_c functions
statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on ℝ^N that is finite on compact sets and let n ∈ ℕ. Suppose that ∫ (n·h(y) + Dh(y)(y)) dμ(y) = 0 for every C¹ function h : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support (Dh = fderiv ℝ h). Then for every C¹ function g : ℝ^N → ℝ with compact support and every s > 0, ∫ g(s⁻¹y) dμ(y) = s^n ∫ g dμ.
lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → (∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∫ y, ((n : ℝ) * g y + fderiv ℝ g y y) ∂μ = 0) → ∀ g : Euclidean N → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∫ y, g (s⁻¹ • y) ∂μ = s ^ n * ∫ y, g y ∂μ
